correctness.rationale: For finite abelian G, real f with S=supp(fhat) contained in the nontrivial coset a+H of index-two H and |S|>2|H|/3: equality of fourth autocorrelations yields equal magnitudes from (s,-s,s,-s) and multiplicative Freiman-two identities r(s1)r(s2)=r(s3)r(s4). If D=(a+H)\S, 3|D|<|H| ensures simultaneous s,s+t,s+t+u in S for all t,u in H, giving well-defined character delta(t)=r(s+t)/r(s). Since -s0 in S, delta(2s0)=r(s0)^2, so delta extends across the index-two coset with value r(s0), and Fourier inversion gives a translate. At |S|=2|H|/3 the Z6 spectrum {1,5} with phases 1 vs (i,-i) has the same zero-sum quartic Fourier products yet is not a translate: i is not a sixth root. Recomputed pair/three-translate intersections for 53682 cyclic test triples and checked all six Z6 quartic products. Finite tests are corroboration, not proof of the all-group assertion.
residual_risks: Real signals only; exactly one nontrivial index-two coset; strict >2/3; exact noiseless fourth autocorrelation; threshold sharp across groups but not each individual group.

value.rationale: This is a natural sharp missing-frequency tolerance for recovering real signals from one fixed fourth-order autocorrelation in an index-two spectral coset. The 1/3 erasure boundary is structural (three-translate consistency) rather than an arbitrary parameter slice, and the counterexample identifies exact failure at the uniform threshold. It is not a stability or algorithmic decoding claim.
